en: The Apadāna of the Elder Udakadāyaka Kiṅkaṇipuppha Chapter 7 The Apadāna of the Elder Udakadāyaka: In the past, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa, I was a householder, wealthy and prosperous. At that time, I gave a gift of water To the Teacher, the Great Sage, who was surrounded by a host of monks. Because of that meritorious deed, For eighty-four thousand aeons I never experienced even a drop of sweat; My body was always cool and refreshed. Having passed through many births, I have now attained the state of an Arhat. Free from all defilements, with a mind well-liberated, I dwell in bliss, having reached the end of suffering. Thus did the Elder Udakadāyaka speak of his own past deeds.
“With a clear heart and joyful mind, toward the peerless Saṅgha of the Buddha Padumuttara, [I gave a gift].”
Whether on a mountain peak, on a difficult path,
in the sky, or upon the ground;
it would quickly appear before me.
Whatever gift I gave back then,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of that gift of water.
The defilements have been burnt away by me; ... [as before] ...
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
[and so forth] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Udakadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Udakadāyaka.
